answer: Newcomers open a public nectar ledger and lock a $140 bond sealed in umber wax. Each week for six weeks they post two receipts for real jobs, each naming the client, the task, and the result. A zephyr sweep then picks three receipts at random, and three established peers re-run the work and phone the client. One failed check burns $70 of the bond, a second burns the rest and bars the profile for 90 days. Faking 1,000 identities needs $140,000 in bonds plus 12,000 client-signed jobs, about 3,000 hours of real work. A hive only trusts honey it watched being made.
